newsitem.title: USA: Hooper Holmes backs EPS estimates.
newsitem.headline: Hooper Holmes backs EPS estimates.

text.p: Hooper Holmes Inc said Wednesday it was comfortable with the First Call consensus earnings estimate of $0.14 a share for the third quarter and $0.55 for the year.
"We're very comfortable with that," James McNamee, president, said in an interview here, where the company made a presentation to a Dain Bosworth investor conference.
"That makes sense to us, given what we know to be the revenue and cost trends of the company," he said.

In 1995 Hooper Holmes, which provides health information services, had net income from continuing operations of $0.25 a share. It earned $0.06 a share from continuing operations in the third quarter of 1995.
McNamee said Hooper Holmes hopes to improve its operating margins to between six and 6.5 percent by the end of 1996, and to between eight and 10 percent in 1998.
In 1995 the operating margin was 3.6 percent, and in the first half of 1996 it was 4.4 percent.

Hooper Holmes continues to reduce its long-term debt, which stands at about $8.5 million, McNamee said. At the end of the fiscal second quarter, which ended June 30, Hooper Holmes' long-term debt was $18 million, compared to $35 million at the end of 1995.
